prompt: A wheelchair ramp rises $2$ ft over a horizontal run of $24$ ft. What angle does the ramp make with the ground? Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
hint: You know the opposite side ($2$) and the adjacent side ($24$) — that pair points to tangent.

hints.text: You know the opposite side ($2$) and the adjacent side ($24$) — that pair points to tangent.
$\tan \theta = \frac{2}{24}$. To get $\theta$ itself, use the inverse tangent, $\tan^{-1}$.

explanation: The rise is opposite the angle and the run is adjacent, so use tangent: $\tan \theta = \frac{2}{24}$.
Undo the tangent with $\tan^{-1}$: $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.08333) \approx 4.76^\circ$, which rounds to $4.8^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the answer should be small
steps: A ramp that climbs only 2 ft while stretching 24 ft is very gradual.
A gentle slope means a small angle, so an answer near $5^\circ$ makes sense — the ADA slope limit is right about here.
